rv.q: What emerges is a wonderfully concise and coherent work of theatre, the roots of which are clear, but the substance very much of their own making, of an intimate space managed perfectly, of women now and not just then.
A phenomenal cast and crisp direction combine to provide an equally hilarious and thoughtful theatrical experience.
But with only lip service paid to the broader social context in which these women lived, much of what could be interesting here dances tantalisingly beneath the surface.
The exceptional writing, direction and performances allow the comedy and tragedy to ebb and flow in a beautiful example of what theatre can achieve.
This warm-hearted adaptation from director Josh Roche offers tender reflections on grief and independence while maximising the laughs.
Lin Coghlan and Shaun McKenna’s adaptation of Elizabeth Gaskell's 'Cranford' balances sharp comedy with tender heartbreak, led by an unforgettable Tamsin Greig.
This is a seasonal offering, and the play’s resolve is utterly heartwarming and elevating.

cn.t: Critics praise this warm-hearted Gaskell adaptation for its humor and poignant reflections on grief, though one finds it lost in Christmas sentimentality. The production earns acclaim for vividly bringing Victorian village life to the stage.
